text:
B: Hi! Hello, can you hear me okay?
A: Yeah. Hiya.
B: I'm Chiara. And you're Liam?
A: Yeah.
B: Lovely. Erm, so where are you?
A: Walsall.
B: Walsall. Okay. Is that near Tipton? I just spoke to Dean, and now I know Tipton.
A: Yeah, next door, sort of. I had Dean earlier as well.
B: Oh, good, so we have a friend in common! I'm in Fulham. So, erm, what do you do?
A: IT. Parcel depot. Nights, mostly.
B: Oh, nights, that's hard. I thought from your photo maybe tech. The fleece, you know. Very... practical.
A: Work fleece, yeah. Just come off a shift.
B: You must be exhausted. Sorry, I'll try not to talk too much. I always talk too much on these.
A: You're alright.
B: Okay. Erm. What do you like, outside work? Sorry, that sounds like a job interview, no?
A: Bit. Er, I fix stuff off Marketplace and sell it on. Graphics cards, laptops, controllers. Buy them broken, cheap, sort them, flip them.
B: Oh, wait, I do that! Not fixing, sorry, but I buy vintage handbags on resale sites. And I'm literally obsessed. I'm watching one now, a nineties Prada, and I check it every morning.
A: Do you sell them on?
B: Sometimes. If I get bored of one. And I can spot a fake at ten paces, honestly. The stitching, the zip, the font on the logo. People try it all the time.
A: Yeah, same with cards. People flash the BIOS so a cheap one shows up as a better model. You've got to check the serial on the board.
B: Exactly! It's the same thing! You have to look at the inside.
A: Yeah. Most people don't bother looking.
B: And do you always describe them perfectly, your listings? Because the sellers I buy from, cioè, "excellent condition" means nothing.
A: [laughs] Er... mostly. "Fully working." If it's working when it leaves mine, that's on them after.
B: [laughs] Okay, that's very honest. I'm not sure it's honest, but it's honest.
A: Yeah.
B: Do you travel? Sorry, I keep asking questions.
A: Tenerife. Twice. Turkey once. All-inclusive, by the pool.
B: Oh, that sounds so relaxing. I'm the opposite, I research every hotel for weeks and then I panic about the flight connections.
A: I just turn up. Wife books it.
B: That's the dream, honestly. Is there somewhere you really want to go?
A: Japan. For the tech, the cars. Akihabara and that. Not happening any time soon, though.
B: Why not?
A: Money. Saving for a house.
B: Yeah. No, I understand. London rent is the same, it eats everything. Does that make sense?
A: Yeah.
B: But Japan you should do one day. Even a short one. My husband went for work, and he said the food alone...
A: Bit far for a short one.
B: True. Okay, true. Erm, and are you enjoying the study? The calls?
A: Yeah, it's alright. Better than I thought.
B: Oh, good! I was nervous with you, actually, I thought—
